newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit tests 2.51, retreats on intervention fear.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit tests 2.51, retreats on intervention fear.

text.p: The ringgit remained in its predicted range after the dollar failed to make a break above the 2.5100 barrier, dealers said on Monday.
Dollar/ringgit tested 2.51/dollar around 0700 GMT, but renewed fears of Bank Negara's intervention forced a sell down, they said.
"There is some speculation that Bank Negara may have checked rates at the 2.5100 level," research firm MMS International said in a report from Singapore.
Many dealers said the central bank was not visible in the market and the 2.51 barrier was only psychological.
Dealers said a rumour about trouble at a stockbroking firm in Malaysia amidst fast-dropping share prices on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange had also caused selling of the ringgit.
"Market talk is that a south (Malaysia)-based securities firm with a largely retail base may suffer 100 million ringgit losses on contract losses suffered by its clients," MMS said.
"It seems that this rumour is not true. It seems the work of those who wanted to offload accumulated dollar positions," said the head of dealing at a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur.
A Singapore-based analyst said dollar/ringgit could head higher in London after the close of the Asian markets.
At 0830 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5070/80.
